title: Cross-Lingual Stability of Safety Circuits in Open Models

original_idea.body:
# Cross-Lingual Stability of Safety Circuits in Open Models

**Problem:** Safety/refusal circuits are studied in English; whether the same feature fires for equivalent harmful prompts in other languages is under-explored.

**Direction:** Locate a refusal/harm feature on a multilingual open model using English, test activation for translated equivalents in 2-3 languages, check if multilingual jailbreaks correspond to feature non-activation.

**Why it matters:** Multilingual safety gaps are a real deployment risk; a mechanistic account is novel and lab-independent.

**Relevant context:** Gemma/Qwen/Aya; TransformerLens/SAELens.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: mechanistic account of multilingual refusal failures targets a real, under-resourced deployment risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Locate a feature and test cross-lingual activation; no training, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused (one feature, 2-3 languages) with a clear activation-gap metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Under-resourced non-English safety, open multilingual weights; neglected, lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on an open multilingual model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Behavioral multilingual gaps documented; the feature-level mechanistic account is the open angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Behavioral gaps are known; the mechanistic feature-level cross-lingual account appears largely open.
